subsystems.name: Catoms (unit modules)
subsystems.role: the repeating cell; each is a tiny robot that must sense, compute, latch and move relative to its neighbours.

subsystems.name: Latching and connection
subsystems.role: hold modules rigidly enough to carry structural load, then release to reconfigure.

subsystems.name: Power distribution
subsystems.role: get energy to every module, including ones buried inside a shape with no external connection.

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: move one module past another — the hardest part, because micron-scale actuators are weak.

subsystems.name: Localisation and sensing
subsystems.role: each module must know where it is and how it sits relative to its neighbours.

subsystems.name: Control software
subsystems.role: translate a commanded global shape into moves that individual modules can carry out locally.

subsystems.name: Fabrication and handling
subsystems.role: make millions of identical modules cheaply and test them.

buildSteps.title: Fix the unit cell
buildSteps.detail: choose a module size (typically quoted between about 1 mm and 1 cm) and split that volume between power, logic, actuation and latch; every increase in size cubes the number of modules a given volume needs.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the modules
buildSteps.detail: the logic and sensors would be made with standard silicon lithography, while actuators, latches and contacts are added by MEMS processes such as deep etching, electroplating and wafer bonding, then diced into individual catoms.

buildSteps.title: Make the faces
buildSteps.detail: each cube face carries conductive pads for power and data plus the latch surfaces; electrical contact must survive thousands of make-and-break cycles in a dusty, humid environment.

buildSteps.title: Solve actuation
buildSteps.detail: modules move by electrostatic or magnetic inchworm steps: surfaces are clamped in sequence so the module walks across its neighbour. Lab demonstrations at centimetre scale have done this with magnetic latching; shrinking to millimetres is unresolved.

buildSteps.title: Add local intelligence
buildSteps.detail: each module runs a small program that reads neighbour states and follows simple local rules, since no central controller can address millions of units in real time.

buildSteps.title: Write the shape compiler
buildSteps.detail: software converts a target 3D shape into sequences of module moves, then simulates whether the moves are physically possible without collisions.

buildSteps.title: Build a first lattice
buildSteps.detail: start with a few hundred centimetre-scale modules making and breaking simple shapes, then scale down module size and up module count.

buildSteps.title: Scale and self-repair
buildSteps.detail: a functioning material needs enough surplus modules that broken ones can be replaced by neighbours shuffling through the structure; this redundancy, not the modules themselves, sets the achievable reliability.

prerequisites.tech: Micro-scale actuators with useful force density
prerequisites.why: electrostatic forces scale badly at small sizes and micro-motors are hard to make with the torque and lifetime needed to move a module carrying its own power and logic.

prerequisites.tech: Power delivery through a reconfigurable body
prerequisites.why: contact pads between modules wear and oxidise, and there is no way to wire a shape that is constantly changing.

prerequisites.tech: Millions-off micro-fabrication at low unit cost
prerequisites.why: semiconductor lines produce billions of transistors cheaply, but complete micro-robots combining logic, power storage and moving parts are far more complex to package and test.
simulated and small-robot demonstrations exist; guaranteeing a target shape emerges from local rules with faulty, lost or jammed modules is unsolved.

prerequisites.tech: High-voltage or high-current drive on chip
prerequisites.why: electrostatic actuation needs hundreds of volts and magnetic latching needs current pulses, both awkward to generate and switch at micron scale.

pathway.milestone: 2D and small 3D self-reconfiguring modular robots at centimetre scale in university laboratories
pathway.unlocks: techniques for latching, neighbour sensing and shape algorithms.

pathway.milestone: centimetre-scale 3D modules with integrated power and computation, in lattices of hundreds
pathway.unlocks: demonstrations of a solid object changing shape under software control.

pathway.milestone: millimetre-scale modules made in quantity, self-assembling into thousands-unit blocks
pathway.unlocks: material thin and fine enough to be useful rather than a sculpture.

pathway.milestone: structures of millions of modules with self-repair and structural load-bearing
pathway.unlocks: walls, furniture and tools that reconfigure on command — speculative, and gated entirely on the actuator and power problems above.
